questions.q: Calculate the arithmetic mean of the given ungrouped data. Use the method 'Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 20, n = 100, total = 360. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 3.6 rupees

questions.q: Find the mean of the following observations. Use the method 'Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 60, n = 8, total = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.625 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)' refers to.
questions.a: The arithmetic mean is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations, giving a single representative value of the data set.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)'.
questions.a: The mean balances the data so that the total of deviations above and below it cancel out.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: mean = sum(x_i) / n

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Median (Ungrouped Data)' refers to.
questions.a: The median is the middle value of an ordered data set that divides the observations into two equal halves, with half the values below and half above it.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Median (Ungrouped Data)'.
questions.a: The median is unaffected by extreme values and is found after arranging data in ascending or descending order.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Median (Ungrouped Data)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: median = middle value (odd n) or average of two middle values (even n)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Mode (Ungrouped Data)' refers to.
questions.a: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set, representing the observation with the highest frequency.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mode (Ungrouped Data)'.
questions.a: A data set may be unimodal (one mode), bimodal (two modes), or have no mode if all values occur equally.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Mode (Ungrouped Data)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: mode = value with maximum frequency

concepts.title: Range as a Measure of Dispersion

questions.q: Calculate the range of the given data. Use the method 'Range as a Measure of Dispersion'. Work with: data_total = 40, max_val = 50, min_val = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 35 rupees

questions.q: Find the spread of the data set using range. Use the method 'Range as a Measure of Dispersion'. Work with: data_total = 200, max_val = 25, min_val = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 7 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Range as a Measure of Dispersion' refers to.
questions.a: Range is the simplest measure of dispersion, defined as the difference between the largest and smallest observations in a data set.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Range as a Measure of Dispersion'.
questions.a: Range gives a quick sense of the spread of data but is highly sensitive to extreme values.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Range as a Measure of Dispersion', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: range = maximum value - minimum value

questions.q: Calculate the standard deviation of the given data. Use the method 'Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 150, n = 20, sum_sq_dev = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.3873 rupees

questions.q: Find the standard deviation for ungrouped observations. Use the method 'Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 60, n = 500, sum_sq_dev = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.0894 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)' refers to.
questions.a: Standard deviation is the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations of each observation from the mean, measuring the absolute dispersion of data around the mean.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)'.
questions.a: A lower standard deviation indicates data points are close to the mean, while a higher value indicates greater spread.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: sigma = sqrt( sum((x_i - mean)^2) / n )

questions.q: Calculate the variance of the given data. Use the method 'Variance (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 400, n = 360, sum_sq_dev = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 0.1389 rupees

questions.q: Find the variance for ungrouped observations. Use the method 'Variance (Ungrouped Data)'. Work with: data_total = 360, n = 10, sum_sq_dev = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 1.5 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Variance (Ungrouped Data)' refers to.
questions.a: Variance is the average of the squared deviations of each observation from the mean, and is the square of the standard deviation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Variance (Ungrouped Data)'.
questions.a: Variance measures the average squared spread of data; it is always non-negative and its unit is the square of the original unit.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Variance (Ungrouped Data)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: variance = sum((x_i - mean)^2) / n

concepts.title: Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI

questions.q: Calculate the index number for the given price data. Use the method 'Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI'. Work with: base_total = 5, current_total = 360, ratio = 30. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 3000 per cent

questions.q: Calculate the CPI for the given basket of goods. Use the method 'Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI'. Work with: base_total = 5, current_total = 120, ratio = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 400 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI' refers to.
questions.a: An index number is a statistical device measuring the relative change in a variable over time with the base period set to 100; the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) tracks wholesale-level price changes while the Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks retail price changes paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI'.
questions.a: Index numbers express changes as percentages relative to a base period; WPI reflects producer-level prices for policy while CPI reflects the cost of living for consumers and is used to adjust wages and pensions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: index_number = (value in current period / value in base period) * 100; CPI = (sum of current retail prices / sum of base retail prices) * 100

concepts.title: Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers

questions.q: Using the method 'Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers', work with: difference = 120, index_current = 25, index_previous = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 800 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers' and work with: difference = 45, index_current = 75, index_previous = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 60 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers' refers to.
questions.a: Inflation is the sustained rise in the general price level over time, measured as the percentage rate of change in a price index such as the CPI or WPI; index numbers are widely used to measure this change, determine purchasing power, deflate monetary values, and guide economic policy and wage adjustments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers'.
questions.a: Index numbers are essential for measuring inflation, which erodes purchasing power; they also help compare economic variables over time, adjust incomes for inflation, and formulate government fiscal and monetary policies.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: inflation_rate = ((CPI_current - CPI_base) / CPI_base) * 100
